algorithms.title: Trie (Prefix Tree Data Structure)
algorithms.summary: Tree structure used for fast string prefix searching, autocomplete, and dictionary lookups.
explanation: Each node contains a map/array of child nodes corresponding to characters (a-z) and a boolean `isEndOfWord`.
Insert word: Walk down matching character nodes. Create new child nodes if absent. Mark last node `isEndOfWord = True`.
Search word: Walk down matching nodes. Return `True` only if last node has `isEndOfWord == True`.
StartsWith prefix: Walk down matching nodes. If all characters found, return `True`.

exampleTrace.output: Search('apple'): True, StartsWith('app'): True, Search('app'): False
traceSteps: Insert('apple'): Create root -> 'a' -> 'p' -> 'p' -> 'l' -> 'e' (set isEnd = True at 'e').
Search('apple'): Traverse 'a'->'p'->'p'->'l'->'e'. Reached 'e', isEnd is True -> Returns True.
StartsWith('app'): Traverse 'a'->'p'->'p'. All nodes exist -> Returns True.
Search('app'): Traverse 'a'->'p'->'p'. Node exists, but isEnd at second 'p' is False -> Returns False.

wAnswers.whatItSolves: Provides fast O(L) string prefix matching independent of total dataset dictionary size N.
wAnswers.whenToUse: When implementing search auto-complete, spell checker, or finding longest common prefix across words.
wAnswers.whereUsed: Google search autocomplete, mobile keyboard predictive text, IP routing longest prefix match.
wAnswers.whyOptimal: Search time depends only on word length L, NOT on total dictionary size N!

algorithms.title: Trie Foundations & Complete Operations (Insert, Search, Delete, Count)
algorithms.timeComplexity: O(L) where L is length of word/prefix
algorithms.spaceComplexity: O(N * L * Σ) for N words of length L over alphabet size Σ
algorithms.summary: Tree-like prefix data structure supporting insert, search, deletion, prefix checking, and frequency counts in O(L) time.
explanation: Trie Node contains an array or HashMap of children pointers `children[26]` and `isEnd` boolean flag.
Insert: Traverse character by character, creating new child nodes if absent. Mark last node `isEnd = True`.
Search: Traverse characters. If any character pointer is null, return False. Else return `curr.isEnd`.
StartsWith (Prefix Search): Similar to search, but returns True as long as prefix traversal succeeds.
Count Words Equal To & Starting With: Store `countEnds` and `countPrefix` counters at each Trie node.

traceSteps: insert('apple'): Root -> 'a' -> 'p' -> 'p' -> 'l' -> 'e' (isEnd=True).
search('apple'): Follow path a-p-p-l-e. Node 'e' has isEnd=True -> Return True.
startsWith('app'): Follow path a-p-p. Path exists -> Return True.

wAnswers.whatItSolves: Provides prefix-based character sequence lookups in linear time proportional to word length.
wAnswers.whenToUse: When storing a large dictionary of strings and performing frequent prefix searches.
wAnswers.whereUsed: Search engine autocomplete, spell checkers, IP routing tables, T9 predictive text.
wAnswers.whyOptimal: Prefix matching takes O(L) time independent of total dictionary size N.

algorithms.title: Word Dictionary with Wildcard Pattern Matching (Dot Search)
algorithms.timeComplexity: O(L) for normal search, O(Σ^L) worst case for wildcard '.' search
algorithms.summary: Implements a word dictionary using Trie that supports '.' wildcard matching to match any single character during search.
explanation: Store words in a standard Trie.
When searching word `s` at index `idx` and node `curr`:
If `char != '.'`: Check if `char` exists in `curr.children` and recursively continue.
If `char == '.'`: Try ALL non-null children of `curr` using backtracking DFS!
If any child returns True, return True.

traceSteps: addWord('bad') and ('dad') into Trie.
search('.ad'): '.' matches both 'b' and 'd'. Branches down 'b' -> 'a' -> 'd' (isEnd=True) -> Return True.
search('b..'): matches 'b' -> '.' matches 'a' -> '.' matches 'd' -> Return True.

wAnswers.whatItSolves: Performs regex-like single character wildcard matching across stored words.
wAnswers.whenToUse: When supporting wildcard pattern searches or crosswords in dictionary systems.
wAnswers.whereUsed: Regex engines, crossword puzzle solvers, command line wildcard search.
wAnswers.whyOptimal: Prunes search branches instantly when literal characters do not match.

algorithms.title: Longest Common Prefix & Autocomplete Engine
algorithms.timeComplexity: O(N * L) construction, O(Prefix + K) search
algorithms.summary: Builds Autocomplete engine suggestions and finds Longest Common Prefix across strings using Trie branching inspection.
explanation: Longest Common Prefix: Insert all strings into Trie.
Traverse from root while node has EXACTLY ONE child and `isEnd == False`.
The accumulated characters form the Longest Common Prefix.
Autocomplete Engine: Navigate to node representing prefix `P`.
Perform DFS/BFS from prefix node to gather all word completions ordered by frequency rating.

traceSteps: Insert 'flower', 'flow', 'flight' into Trie.
Root child count = 1 ('f'). Add 'f' to prefix.
Node 'f' child count = 1 ('l'). Add 'l' to prefix.
Node 'l' child count = 2 ('o' and 'i'). Branching detected -> Stop!
Longest Common Prefix = 'fl'.

wAnswers.whatItSolves: Generates real-time top autocomplete recommendations and prefix overlaps.
wAnswers.whenToUse: When providing search suggestions or identifying shared string prefixes.
wAnswers.whereUsed: Google search bar autocomplete, IDE code completion (IntelliSense), mobile keyboard auto-suggest.
wAnswers.whyOptimal: Narrows candidate recommendations to the prefix subtree in O(Prefix) time.

algorithms.title: Word Search II (Grid Search with Trie Pruning)
algorithms.timeComplexity: O(M * N * 4^L) with instant Trie prefix pruning
algorithms.summary: Searches for all words from a dictionary present in a 2D grid using 4-directional Backtracking optimized by Trie prefix pruning.
explanation: Build Trie from target dictionary words.
Iterate through every cell `(r, c)` in 2D grid.
Perform DFS/Backtracking on cell `(r, c)` matching against Trie pointers.
Pruning Optimization: If current grid character is NOT in Trie children, prune search branch immediately!
When a word end is reached in Trie, add to result list and clear `isEnd = False` (or remove word node) to prevent duplicates.

traceSteps: Build Trie for ['oath', 'pea', 'eat', 'rain'].
Start DFS at board[0][0] ('o'): matches Trie 'o' -> 'a' -> 't' -> 'h' (word 'oath' found!).
Start DFS at board[1][2] ('e'): matches Trie 'e' -> 'a' -> 't' (word 'eat' found!).
Prune paths for 'pea' and 'rain' when character paths fail in Trie.
Returned words: ['eat', 'oath'].

wAnswers.whatItSolves: Searches thousands of dictionary words simultaneously in a 2D letter grid.
wAnswers.whenToUse: When performing multi-word 2D board searches (Boggle games).
wAnswers.whereUsed: Boggle game solvers, 2D matrix pattern search engines.
wAnswers.whyOptimal: Trie prefix pruning eliminates billions of invalid DFS grid paths instantly.

algorithms.title: Bitwise Binary Trie (Maximum & Minimum XOR Pair)
algorithms.summary: Bitwise 32-bit (or 31-bit) Binary Trie (0/1 branching) used to calculate Maximum XOR or Minimum XOR pair in an array in linear O(N) time.
explanation: Binary Trie: Each node has 2 children `child[0]` (bit 0) and `child[1]` (bit 1).
Insert: Convert number to 31-bit binary representation (MSB to LSB, i.e. bit 30 down to 0).
Find Maximum XOR for x: For each bit `b` of x, greedily try to traverse OPPOSITE bit `1 - b` in Trie!
If `1 - b` child exists, take it (yielding a 1 bit in XOR result) and update `current_xor |= (1 << i)`.
Else: Must take `b` child.

traceSteps: Insert binary representations of [3, 10, 5, 25, 2, 8] into 31-bit Binary Trie.
Query 5 (binary 00101): Greedily pick opposite bit 1 at MSB bit position 4 (25 is binary 11001).
Maximum XOR = 28.

wAnswers.whatItSolves: Finds Maximum XOR pair or Maximum XOR subarray in O(N * 31) time.
wAnswers.whenToUse: When maximizing/minimizing bitwise XOR combinations across array elements.
wAnswers.whereUsed: Cryptography XOR keys, digital signal encoding, competitive programming bitwise queries.
wAnswers.whyOptimal: Greedy MSB-first binary Trie traversal guarantees maximum possible XOR value.

algorithms.title: Compressed Trie & Radix Tree (Patricia Trie)
algorithms.summary: Space-optimized Trie variant (Radix Tree / Patricia Trie) that compresses non-branching single-child paths into single multi-character edge labels.
explanation: Standard Trie Issue: Single child chains (e.g. 't' -> 'e' -> 's' -> 't') waste node pointers.
Compressed Trie (Radix Tree): Merges single-child nodes so edge labels store full strings (e.g. edge label 'test').
Node Reduction: Number of nodes is bounded by O(N) where N is number of stored words.
Lookup: Compare prefix strings along edge labels. Split edges during insertion if prefix partially matches.
Widely used in IP routing (longest prefix matching) and Linux file system inodes.

traceSteps: Insert 'tester': Root edge 'tester'.
Insert 'testing': Common prefix 'test'. Split edge: Root -> 'test' -> ['er', 'ing'].
Insert 'slow' & 'slower': Common prefix 'slow'. Split edge: Root -> 'slow' -> ['', 'er'].
Compressed node count is 5 (vs 20 nodes in standard Trie!).

wAnswers.whatItSolves: Drastically reduces node pointer memory overhead in sparse Tries.
wAnswers.whenToUse: When storing long strings or IP address prefixes with sparse branching.
wAnswers.whereUsed: Linux kernel Page Cache, Router IP lookup tables (CIDR prefix matching), HTTP router URL matching.
wAnswers.whyOptimal: Bounds total tree node count to at most 2N-1 nodes regardless of key lengths.
